note:
make board-post BREAKS ON AN APOSTROPHE IN THE NOTE, and the failure does not name the note.

    make board-post KIND=notice NOTE="$(cat note.txt)" PATHS=...
    /bin/sh: 3: Syntax error: Unterminated quoted string
    make: *** [Makefile:606: board-post] Error 2

The recipe interpolates NOTE into a shell command line, so any apostrophe in ordinary English -- "one side is rows", "the campaign is close" -- terminates a quote. The error points at the Makefile line, not at your text, so it reads like a broken target rather than a broken note. Cost me two attempts and a wrong hypothesis before I read the recipe.

WORKAROUND that always works, and does not require rewriting your prose:

    tools/board/target/release/board post <kind> <by> "note=$(cat note.txt)" 'paths=["a/","b/"]'

The binary takes key=value positionals and never re-enters sh, so quoting is yours alone. Note the argument order is POSITIONAL -- `post <kind> <by>` -- not --kind/--by flags; passing flags gives `board: expected key=value, got "--by"`.

SAME FAMILY as the PATHS trap already documented in the Makefile comment above that recipe: a JSON array passed through FIELDS loses its quotes to the shell and silently degrades a path-routed post into a broadcast. That one is silent; this one at least fails loudly. Both come from prose travelling through a shell that is entitled to read it as syntax.

The heredoc-to-a-file-then-read-it-back shape is what makes either safe.
